verdict.pair_reasons:
X vs Y — Y wins on verified substance. Y is the only output that found hooks/dispatch-assert.sh:225, hooks/dispatch-assert.sh:258 and hooks/handoff-claim-assert.sh:127 (I confirmed the byte-identical `jq -nc --arg r "$reason" '{decision:"block",reason:$r}'` at all three, :225 inside the `if [ -f "$PENDING" ]` re-check arm), and consequently the only one that answers Q4 correctly — X states flatly 'All four files are registered, so none is missing', which is false: both files are absent from every JSON in the repo and are wired only by docs/activation/pending-activation/11-dispatch-assert-activate.sh (Y quotes :21-22 byte-exactly) and migrations/0027-handoff-claim-registration.sh (Y cites :2 = '# migration-class: c10'). That is a 5-item key deficit on the part of the brief that says 'the site list IS the answer'. X's compensating strength — a much fuller Q5 (~14 drifts, every one of which I verified true, including two I checked independently: completion-assert.sh:177's session-continue :187-208 pointer, real KILL_RE at :348, and :189's ':157-160' pointer, real extractor at :243-246) — is real but does not outweigh missing three sites and mis-answering Q4. X also carries four off-by-one citing-line errors, all in completion-assert.sh (663/695/724/171 should be 662/694/723/170).

X vs Z — tie. Both enumerate the same 7 sites, miss the same 3, and answer Q4 the same wrong way (Z hedges it to 'the files I found', X does not). Their error profiles are comparable in size and opposite in kind: X has four off-by-one citing-line numbers that each still point within a line of a real, verified drift; Z has one fabricated finding — it reports waiting-recycle.sh ':1186 says ":480 abstains no-jq first"' and calls the citation stale, when in fact the citing line is 723, line 480 IS the no-jq abstain (the citation is correct), and 1186 is `rsspaged_for()` — plus two verbatim misquotes, one of them on line 502, the exact evidence line for key item T5 (Z quotes line 501's text; X quotes 502 byte-exactly). Each found genuine drifts the other missed: Z found session-continue.sh:990→completion-assert.sh:99-105 (real resolution at :142-143), completion-assert.sh:1048→:705 (real comment at :1010-1011), and the memory-nudge.sh:26 pointer in two files (real GC at :61); X found completion-assert.sh:177 and :189, plus a fully verified exclusion census (operator-readout 1577/1623/1663, teammate-checkpoint's eight bare exits, subagent-stop's file-only writes, hook-chain's unwired rank_of, relay-verbatim's PostToolUse-only object) and the correct observation that mailbox-wake-arm.sh:5 is a Stop hook registered outside the template with no qualifying site. No single difference is decisive in either direction.

Y vs Z — Y wins. Same 5-item key gap as X vs Y (three sites plus T3 and T4, with Y's staged-registration citations verified verbatim), and Y carries no fabricated findings while Z asserts a stale citation in waiting-recycle.sh that I confirmed is correct, having swapped its two line numbers. Y additionally verified the exclusion of the four variable-driven `decision` writers (reset-hard-shadow-allow.sh:164, curl-gate.py:174, model-permission-decider.py:515, validate-bash.sh:137 — all log-file writes, values never 'block'; model-permission-decider's stdout emit() at :456 writes permissionDecision under PreToolUse), which I checked and which no other output attempted, and found one drift nobody else did (dispatch-assert.sh:41's 'house pattern: completion-assert.sh:22-26', real text at :89-91). Z's advantage is a broader Q5 with three drifts Y missed; that is real but smaller than the site-list and Q4 deficit plus the invented finding.
